title: MCP server module fails to import under the resolved SDK (mcp 2.0.0)
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp/server.py:267 uses @server.list_tools(); pyproject.toml declares mcp>=1.28,<3 so a fresh install resolves 2.0.0 (confirmed latest on PyPI), which removed the low-level decorator API -> _factual.json/_runtime.json report AttributeError: 'Server' object has no attribute 'list_tools'. The decorator API IS present in the locally installed mcp 1.28.1 (lowlevel/server.py:440), so the code is not hallucinated — it is version-incompatible with 2.0.0.
suggestion: Pin mcp>=1.28,<2 (the version whose decorator API this code targets), or register handlers via the 2.0 API (add_request_handler) so import survives on both generations.

title: Protocol tests validate an in-test StubServer, not the real MCP SDK
evidence: tests/test_server.py:10-74 installs a hand-rolled StubServer that re-implements the removed 1.x decorator API whenever mcp is unimportable, then asserts against it. This is why test_coverage=0.94 is green while the real server cannot start — the one broken part of the deliverable is never exercised against the actual SDK.
suggestion: Add a test that imports the module with the real installed mcp and asserts server.run wiring, so an SDK-incompatible break fails CI instead of passing against a stub.

title: MCP server is structurally complete: 16 tools + 1 resource + entrypoint
evidence: server.py:262 Server(); :56-219 sixteen TOOL_DEFINITIONS; :267 list_tools, :273 call_tool, :287 list_resources, :300 read_resource; :315-334 run()/main(); pyproject console script brazilian-soccer-mcp. R1's structural how_to_verify (entrypoint + registered tools/resources exist) is fully met; the runtime break is scored by the factual/runtime gates, not requirement_coverage.
suggestion: None — R1 counts as implemented for requirement_coverage. The overall run still fails on factual_accuracy=0.0.
